evidence: Matching the free-text "Failed to authenticate" across stdout+stderr is fragile, but the reviewer's remedy (a documented auth error code) does not exist: the agent's probe shows the JSON envelope has terminal_reason "api_error" and api_error_status null for the auth refusal. Parsing the envelope and reading the named `result` field, with every unrecognised refusal dying loudly, keeps the useful half of the finding and makes any future rewording fail loud rather than pass.
guidance_note: When a probe has to classify a CLI's failure, request its structured output format first and branch on parsed fields, falling back to message text only inside the parsed envelope.

evidence: The reviewer hedged its own claim ("uncertain: --tools \"\" may make trust moot"). The agent reported that a live probe from a fresh mktemp dir returned `ok`, exit 0, and the F1 thread's probes from the same kind of dir returned parsed result envelopes, which they could not have done if print mode stopped at the trust dialog. The code stayed as it was, and the verified fact was added to the comment.

The new horizon_auth_state calls mktemp and rm, and login.sh reaches it (directly and through horizon_assert_authenticated) while declaring only claude/mkdir/python3/tmux. lib.sh's own contract says callers declare the tools they reach. Calling horizon_need_base, as run-loop.sh already does, is the fix that contract asks for.
guidance_note: When a shared lib function gains a new external command, grep that function's callers and check each script's horizon_need declarations in the same commit.

narrative: All three findings landed in round 0 on the original diff and were handled in one fix commit, 1321289. The agent tested the reviewer's premises against the real CLI on both F1 and F2: on F1 it found the suggested structured error code did not exist and built a narrower fix, and on F2 it showed the trust-gate worry did not apply. Round 1 approved with no findings.
guidance_observations: Probing the real CLI before answering settled two findings on facts rather than on argument, and kept a wrong default and a needless code change out of the PR.

evidence: The diff replaced the only `cat > ... <<EOF` with horizon_write_marketplace's python3 heredoc. That left `horizon_need cat` in place and left lib.sh's comment saying cat is still reached from pin-instrument.sh. The agent grepped the reachable files and found no remaining cat call, then removed both.
guidance_note: When a change removes the last call to an external tool, grep for that tool's horizon_need line and any comment that justifies it, and remove them in the same change.

narrative: There was one S1 finding: a precheck and a comment left stale because the PR's own rewrite removed the last cat invocation. The agent confirmed it with a grep, fixed it in b7bda5f, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: Removing a tool's last use without sweeping its declaration is a small, predictable leftover that a pre-push grep would catch.

evidence: readPending's catch has a non-ENOENT branch, `unusable('could not be read (...)')`, and the original tests covered only the parse-failure and missing-field shapes. 7c23490 adds a directory-in-place-of-file shape (EISDIR) under both choices, and the agent reported a mutation check showing those cases fail if the branch rethrows.
guidance_note: When adding a new failure branch to a parser, add one test per branch, including the read-error branch, before pushing.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. Named fix 7c23490 changed only laws-switch.test.js, while the tmp+`mv -f` write in skill-router.sh belongs to the original PR (its subject is "the guard writes it atomically"), so round 0 missed it. The premise holds: `mv src existing-dir` moves the file into the directory and exits 0, where the old redirect failed. The agent correctly refused the suggested `rm -rf` of a directory it did not create and put a `[ ! -d ... ]` precondition first, so the existing could-not-record branch withholds the offer.
guidance_note: When replacing a `>` redirect with write-temp-then-mv, list the destination states (absent, file, directory, symlink) and check each one, because mv onto a directory behaves differently from a redirect.

narrative: Round 0 found a missing test for a new read-error branch, fixed in 7c23490. Round 1 found the mv-into-directory behaviour in the PR's original atomic-write change. The flag ties that finding to the test-only fix commit, but the fix did not touch that code. The agent's different fix avoided a destructive rm -rf and came with a router test, and round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: Both findings were gaps in the original diff that enumerating edge shapes would have caught; no fix introduced a new defect.

evidence: The YAML/TOML gap is real, but it predates the PR (the agent dates it to at least 2.1.259), and the reviewer's first remedy would not work: `Bun.YAML.parse(text)` has no `?.` on the call, so an empty namespace turns the crash into "not a function". The agent took the reviewer's second option, a doc justification. 4ea98de states why an empty namespace would not help and names the tracking ticket promptctl-injector-jeq.

The flag is a false positive. 4ea98de changed only SEAMS.md, and `unsafe: namespace('unsafe', {})` is in the original diff. The duplication is real, and the name it repeats is what the launcher shows the user. Deriving the name from the key through Object.entries, with a test that reads a missing member from a second namespace, removes the duplication.
guidance_note: When a helper takes a name that must equal the key it is assigned to, derive the name from the key at the outset instead of passing a parallel string literal.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. 4ea98de was a doc-only change, and the `key in target` trap is original code. Inherited Object.prototype members are not stubs if real Bun's namespace objects inherit them too, and reporting `toString`/`constructor` as absent would name APIs Bun has. Mirroring the top-level surface Proxy's rule keeps the two consistent, and the noise concern had already been weighed and declined in the local low pass (issue comment).

narrative: Round 0 raised a pre-existing YAML/TOML gap. The agent correctly showed the suggested empty-namespace remedy would not stop the crash and documented why. Round 1's two findings carry ON-POST-REVIEW flags for a SEAMS.md-only commit, but both are on original bun-surface.js code: one real duplication, fixed by deriving names from keys, and one prototype-member objection, correctly declined. Round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: The local low pass had already raised and reasoned through the Proxy-key question, so the reviewer's F3 was answered consistently with a recorded prior decision.

evidence: The flag is a false positive for fix-causation. Rounds 0-7 never finished, so there was no earlier finding for 202a957 to fix. The ROUTE_TEXT reduction came from an owner commit (patch-id 56fcb1d3) that the owner then confirmed, so declining to restore it was right. Deleting tests 15a-d left no test on the session-start emission, which was real and was fixed in ee8d879, and that fix also quoted the heredoc to remove a `$` expansion hazard.
guidance_note: When deleting a function together with its tests, add at least one test for the behaviour that remains on the same output path, so the emission is never left untested.

evidence: This came from the PR's own SKILL.md rewrite, not from a fix for an earlier finding. 202a957 does not touch SKILL.md, and no earlier findings existed. guidance_note: When writing about a policy whose own header disowns a term, grep the new prose for that term before pushing.

evidence: This came from the PR's original body rewrite, not from a fix: no earlier finding existed, and 202a957 does not touch this file. The diff hunk shows the `---`/name/description frontmatter deleted, which removes the skill from discovery. The agent restored it in ee8d879 with a description fitted to the new body.
guidance_note: After rewriting any SKILL.md, diff its first lines against master and confirm the frontmatter block survived.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. cf65b8f only reflowed header lines 16-21, and the truncated INPUT comment ("Every hook event delivers JSON on stdin", no period) already sat in the round-8 head from the owner's comment rewrite, which round 8 did not flag. The premise holds: json_field uses a line-oriented `grep -oE`, so the `tr -d '\n'` is load-bearing. 0b12280 restores the reason.
guidance_note: When a finding points at one casualty of a bulk rewrite passing through the branch, sweep every comment that rewrite deleted for other load-bearing explanations in the same fix.

evidence: The flag points at 0b12280, which touched only skill-router.sh, but the agent admits this was its own regression. f7354f3 generalized the plugin entry's "(code / prose / prompt)" in answer to a local /code-review medium finding and left marketplace.json line 3 naming the three media. guidance_note: When generalizing one copy of an enumerated list, grep every metadata file, including other fields in the same file, for the same enumeration before pushing the fix.

narrative: Rounds 0-7 and 9 and 11 are unfinished runs (rate limits or SIGINT), so the real reviews are rounds 8, 10, 12, 13 and 14. Round 8's three findings were on the PR's original rewrite: a gutted routing text that the owner had authored and confirmed, deleted frontmatter, and "pairs" wording. Round 12 caught a load-bearing comment that the owner's rewrite had dropped. Round 13's F5 came from the agent's own incomplete metadata sweep in f7354f3 (a local-review fix), and the extra approval round 14 is the one avoidable round.
guidance_observations: Fixes driven by local /code-review passes produce reviewer findings with no packet finding id to name as their cause. F5 is one, so fix-caused rounds here undercount.

An owner commit carried through a feature branch got reviewed as the agent's work. Checking that commit's collateral (dropped comments, frontmatter) once, up front, would have folded F4 into the round-8 response.
